questions.q: Why are the features of this regression easy to build for the future?
options: They depend only on the date
They depend on the future target
They are random
They use the last forecast
why: Correct: time index, Fourier terms and holidays are all functions of the calendar.
The future target is unknown.
Random features would have no use.
That describes a recursive model, not this one.

questions.q: Daily data, weekly Fourier terms with K = 3 and yearly Fourier terms with K = 5. How many Fourier columns in total?
A changepoint column max(0, t - 100) has weight -0.3. What is the meaning?
options: The slope of the trend decreases by 0.3 per step after t = 100
The level drops by 0.3 at t = 100
The season changes by 0.3
The series ends at t = 100
why: Correct: the column grows by 1 per step after 100, so its weight is a change of slope.
A level jump would use a step column that is 0 before and 1 after.
A season is built from Fourier terms.
The column continues after 100.

questions.q: Which period P do you use for the yearly Fourier terms on daily data?
questions.why: One year has about 365.25 days (including leap years).

questions.q: Your regression forecast is worse than seasonal naive on a backtest, and the residuals still have autocorrelation. What can you do?
options: Add AR terms or model the residuals with ARIMA
Delete the Fourier terms
Add 50 more harmonics
Remove the test set
why: Correct: leftover autocorrelation is information that recent values can use.
The Fourier terms catch the season. Deleting them loses that.
Many harmonics would overfit.
Removing the test set hides the problem.

questions.q: A shop has a sale in the last week of every November (the date moves with the weekday of Black Friday). What is the right feature?
options: A dummy column that is 1 on the actual sale dates of each year, also for future years
A Fourier term with period 365.25 and K = 1
Nothing, the model will learn it
A feature with last year's sales
why: Correct: the date moves, so list the real dates. A dummy learns the effect.
A smooth wave cannot represent a sharp short peak.
A smooth model does not learn a short sharp event without a feature.
Last year's target would misalign when the date moves.

questions.q: What does Prophet add on top of plain least squares on these features?
options: Bayesian regularisation, many changepoints and uncertainty intervals
A deep neural network
Recursive forecasting
Automatic data collection
why: Correct: it shrinks changepoint weights and gives intervals by simulation.
Prophet is not a neural network.
It does not forecast recursively.
It does not collect data.
